title: Global alignment can exhaust all iterations without converging and still publish a micrograph (e10216-01)
body:
**Status: filed only.** The behaviour is shared with the CPU path (inherited from RELION `ad0b230`). No threshold, iteration-count or publication change has been made or proposed as a PR; this needs the maintainer's decision.

## Result

Movie `e10216-01` (EMPIAR-10216, `FoilHole_14961496_Data_14966722_14966723_20180615_1742_Fractions.mrc`, sha256 `c3b841e9…165ca1`) fails global alignment on CPU and CUDA because it drifts about 12–16 px per frame for the whole exposure, which is far beyond what the global CCF can find. MotionCor3 also fails on it. MotionCorr discards the global "not converged" result and publishes a micrograph with exit status 0. The only warning is a local-fit message on stderr.

## Cause: the movie (measured, except where marked)

Compared with a normal 10216 movie (`e10216-00`, `…_1739_…`) on the raw frames (4GPUs, `taskset` 96-103):

- **Nothing is wrong with the frames themselves.** Per-frame mean is 24.7–25.5 and std 23.0–23.3, against 24.6–25.5 and 22.9–23.4 for `e10216-00`. The zero-pixel fraction is about 5% in both. There are no empty, saturated or duplicated frames: the fraction of pixels equal to the previous frame is at most 1.9%, about chance for these counts.
- **The drift differs.** Consecutive-frame CCF on the unaligned frames (2× binned, band-passed, unrestricted peak search) in `e10216-00` shows frame 1→2 about 20–37 px, then steps of a few px that decay. A clear peak is found in 57 of 58 pairs. In `e10216-01` the steps are a constant ~(dy +12, dx −8…−14) px from frame 2→3 onward, and a clear peak (peak/second-peak > 1.2) is found in only 24 of 58 pairs. Frame 1→2 has no peak (ratio 1.01).
- **Size of the drift.** A prediction-guided tracker (diagnostic, not an aligner; low confidence in the tail) gives about (+670, −625) px between frames 1 and 59, against about 38 px for `e10216-00`. At 0.517 Å/px a 12 px step is about 6 Å per frame.
- **Frame-sum signal.** Thon-ring contrast in the 0.04–0.14 cycle/px band of the plain sum is 0.013 for `e10216-01` and 0.041 for `e10216-00`. After aligning with my tracked trajectory it stays at 0.013 (`e10216-00`: 0.046). I did not separate "my trajectory is imprecise" from "6 Å of motion inside each frame blurs the signal". Either way this movie has no high-resolution signal that alignment is known to recover.
- **Why the CCF fails (inferred from the code).** Each frame is correlated against the sum of the other frames, and the peak is searched only within ±50 px (`search_range = 50`). With ~600 px of drift the reference is smeared, and the per-frame offsets are outside the window. The log is consistent with this: iteration 1 RMSD is 49–50 px on both backends, which is what random peaks inside a ±50 px window give. Normal movies show 21–36 px, then below 1 px in iteration 2–3.
- **Pre-correction control.** I rolled each frame by the smoothed tracked trajectory (integer `np.roll`, window 7; wrap-around seams) and ran the unmodified production CUDA binary (`build-prod-nvcomp`, GPU 0). The original reproduces the sweep exactly (global RMSD 49.13, 68.27, 66.02, 63.90, 62.17 px). The pre-shifted movie gives 18.76, 7.81, 3.90, 4.96, 1.29 px: much closer, still not converged at 5 iterations. So removing the large drift lets the existing algorithm start converging. It does not prove that the full-window search is the only limit; patches still fail (RMSD ~30 px).

## Independent tool: MotionCor3 also fails (measured)

Upstream MotionCor3 1.2.4 (`MotionCor3-stock`, GPU 0), matched settings: `-PixSize 0.517 -kV 300 -FmDose 1.0 -Bft 150 150 -Group 1 1 -FmRef 1 -SumRange 0 0 -Cs 0 -Throw 0 -Trunc 0`, no gain.

| Movie | Setting | Iteration error (px) |
|---|---|---|
| `e10216-00` | `-Iter 5 -Tol 0.5` | 35.3, 0.72, 0.27 (converged at 3) |
| `e10216-01` | `-Iter 5 -Tol 0.5` | 177.2, 176.5, 176.2, 176.1, 167.2 |
| `e10216-01` | `-Iter 15 -Tol 0.1` | stays at 155–177 for all 15 iterations |

The trajectories from the 5- and 15-iteration runs disagree (frame 59: (−101, 164) vs (108, 92)). The patch runs (`-Patch 5 5`) also fail on every patch of `e10216-01`. So the failure is not specific to MotionCorr. RELION's own `relion_run_motioncorr` was not run; the code check below shows the same algorithm.

## Publication path

Shared code, current `main` at `3691374`:

- CPU: [`alignPatch(…, true)` call](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/3691374061f782bc84531fd1c79d017ddcb5a7c2/src/motioncorr_runner.cpp#L3371) discards the `bool` result. CUDA: [`alignPatchDevice(…, true, arena, …)`](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/3691374061f782bc84531fd1c79d017ddcb5a7c2/src/motioncorr_runner.cpp#L3367) discards it too. Whatever is in `xshifts`/`yshifts` is written to the STAR and used for the correction at L3372–3375.
- The decision is a single test, `rmsd < tolerance` with `tolerance = 0.5`: [CPU L4854](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/3691374061f782bc84531fd1c79d017ddcb5a7c2/src/motioncorr_runner.cpp#L4854), [CUDA L685](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/3691374061f782bc84531fd1c79d017ddcb5a7c2/src/acc/cuda/cuda_alignpatch.cu#L685). If the loop runs out of `max_iter` (default 5, [L210](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/3691374061f782bc84531fd1c79d017ddcb5a7c2/src/motioncorr_runner.cpp#L210)), it returns `false` and keeps the last accumulated shifts.
- The search window is [`search_range = 50`](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/3691374061f782bc84531fd1c79d017ddcb5a7c2/src/motioncorr_runner.cpp#L4678) on the CPU and [the same constant](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/3691374061f782bc84531fd1c79d017ddcb5a7c2/src/acc/cuda/cuda_alignpatch.cu#L69) on CUDA.
- Only CUDA logs the outcome ([`[CUDA Global Alignment] completed; converged=no`](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/3691374061f782bc84531fd1c79d017ddcb5a7c2/src/acc/cuda/cuda_alignpatch.cu#L1093)); the CPU log has only the five RMSD lines. Nothing acts on either.
- Local alignment: a non-converged patch is skipped ([L3812](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/3691374061f782bc84531fd1c79d017ddcb5a7c2/src/motioncorr_runner.cpp#L3812)). With no usable patch, `too few valid local trajectories to fit local motion model` goes to **stderr** ([L3856](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/3691374061f782bc84531fd1c79d017ddcb5a7c2/src/motioncorr_runner.cpp#L3856)) and the global trajectory is applied. It is not in the per-movie log, the STAR or the exit status.
- Result for this movie (retained 5×5 runs, PR #243 `raw-4GPUs.tar.gz`): both backends exit 0 and publish the micrograph and a STAR whose frame 2 has Y shift 64.9 px (CPU) and 64.3 px (CUDA). Nothing in the STAR marks the movie as non-converged.
- RELION `ad0b230` is the same: [global `alignPatch` call with the result ignored (L1512)](https://github.com/3dem/relion/blob/ad0b230ca22095700f6392479326836efb1c911d/src/motioncorr_runner.cpp#L1512), [`search_range = 50` (L2282)](https://github.com/3dem/relion/blob/ad0b230ca22095700f6392479326836efb1c911d/src/motioncorr_runner.cpp#L2282), [`tolerance = 0.5` (L2283)](https://github.com/3dem/relion/blob/ad0b230ca22095700f6392479326836efb1c911d/src/motioncorr_runner.cpp#L2283). Only the per-patch result is used there (L1595).

## Options for the maintainer (none implemented)

Each changes behaviour that is shared with the CPU path and RELION, so each needs sign-off.

1. **Report only.** Write `converged=no` to the CPU log as the CUDA path already does, and add a flag to the STAR/`corrected_micrographs.star`. Output is unchanged. The smallest change.
2. **Refuse.** Treat a non-converged global alignment as a movie failure: non-zero exit or a failed-movie record, with no published micrograph. This changes what existing users get for such movies.
3. **Retry.** For example, pre-shift by a coarse estimate or search a wider window and re-run global alignment. This changes algorithm behaviour (and the `ad0b230` parity); on this movie the pre-correction control suggests it can help but did not converge in 5 iterations.
4. **Do nothing**, and document that exit status 0 does not imply convergence.

The question of whether `search_range` or the iteration limit should change is separate and untouched here.

## Evidence and limitations

- Hosts and scratch: 4GPUs, `/mnt/clathrin/alex-motioncorr-e10216-01/` (scripts `inspect_movie.py`, `track_drift.py`, `preshift.py`, `run_mc3.sh`, `run_mcorr.sh`; JSON/logs in `out/`, `mc3/`, `mcorr-orig/`, `mcorr-preshift/`). Movie statistics ran on 4GPUs, not cpu64, because the 2 GB input cannot practically be copied between hosts. They ran under `taskset` 96-103 and used no GPU.
- Not measured: that `search_range` alone limits the fit (needs a source-modified build, not made here); a drift trajectory validated against ground truth; RELION `relion_run_motioncorr` on this movie.
- One normal comparison movie (`e10216-00`) for the statistics and MotionCor3; the sweep's 9 other 10216 movies align normally.

Related: #11, #238, #262; PR #243, PR #261.
